findings.title: A collector feeding records incrementally gets session documents that keep changing after they are returned: session_result hands out the live skill-use counter

evidence.value: skillUses is the running state uses dict itself: the doc holds a reference to the running state, not a snapshot
agent_summary returns rejects as the running state rejects list itself (same aliasing)
new_session, add_record(Skill a:b), r1 = session_result(...) with count 1, then add_record(a second Skill a:b): the r1 doc now shows count 2, and r1 skillUses is state uses -> True
a reader that follows a transcript as it grows can feed records one at a time (new_session / add_record, new_agent / add_agent) and derive exactly what export_sessions.py writes

findings.impact: The stated purpose of the module (D-2, FR-86/FR-87) is an incremental reader that feeds records and derives repeatedly. A collector that keeps the previous result to detect changes, or stores it before feeding more lines, will see skillUses (and an agent summary rejects list) change under it, so a changed skill count can compare equal to the previous document and never be pushed, and earlier stored records are silently rewritten. The v1 exporters are unaffected: they derive once per parse, which is why the byte-identical check passes.
findings.remediation: Have session_result return a snapshot (copy each per-skill dict for skillUses) and have agent_summary return a copy of the rejects list; exporter output bytes are unchanged, since the exporters derive once. Alternatively state plainly in the docstrings that results alias the running state and must be copied before feeding more records. Add a direct test in tests/test_derive.py that derives, feeds another record and asserts the first result is unchanged.
refs: Broken invariant: a returned record must be a snapshot of the state it was derived from
CWE-374 Passing Mutable Objects to an Untrusted Method (closest analogue)

findings.title: export_sessions keeps a use_skill wrapper that nothing calls, a leftover that suggests patching it still affects parsing when it no longer does

evidence.value: def use_skill(uses, sid, skill, ts): derive.use_skill(uses, sid, skill, ts, warn)
Grep over exporters/, tests/, local/: no call to export_sessions.use_skill; derive.add_record calls derive.use_skill directly (derive.py:436, 449). Not a D-3 name (no suite imports or patches it).

findings.impact: Dead code. Before the change parse_session called this module-level use_skill, so a patch on it took effect; now it is bypassed, so the wrapper reads as a hook that silently does nothing.
findings.remediation: Remove the wrapper, or, if it is kept as interface, re-export derive.use_skill in the from-derive import list like the other moved names and note that it is not on the parsing path.

findings.title: The direct tests skip several collector-facing entry points and never exercise feed-derive-feed, the pattern the module exists for

evidence.value: No direct test of derive.carried, derive.project_doc, derive.excluded, derive.verifier_outcome / verdict_of / kind_of, derive.add_agent / new_agent on their own, or usage_doc limit grouping; test_a_session_fed_record_by_record (line 123) derives only once, after all records.

The existing exporter suites exercise these same function objects through export_sessions (e.g. es.carried at tests/test_export_sessions.py:286-294) and main(), so v1 behaviour is covered; the gap is D-5 direct-import coverage and the incremental contract.

findings.impact: PBI-019 will import these functions directly. Without direct tests of project_doc and carried and a feed-derive-feed case, a regression in the collector-only path (such as CR-PBI004-01) is not caught by any suite.
findings.remediation: Add small direct tests for project_doc (linked sessions, counts, aggregated usage), carried (running to killed at the window edge), excluded, and verdict_of on the ver lane; add a test that derives, feeds another record and derives again, asserting the first result is unchanged and the second matches a one-shot parse. The import-purity probe and its self-test (lines 57-75) are sound and need no change.

follow_ups: Error-order note (builder-raised) is acceptable, not a finding: spec_tabs now reads the ADR files and review notes before parsing the spec, so when both fail at once a different error surfaces first. The one case where the exit code also changes is a spec-parse ValueError together with an OSError (e.g. PermissionError) on an ADR or review file: base exited 2 with nothing exported, now the OSError is uncaught (exit 1, traceback). refresh.py treats any non-zero exporter exit the same (refresh.py:90, push nothing) and output bytes are unaffected, so it is within behaviour unchanged; record it in the PBI evidence.

For PBI-019: the running state from new_session holds a set (skillCalls) and may use None as a dict key (launched, stopped, sync), so it is not JSON-serialisable. If the collector must persist derivation state across restarts to honour FR-86 (read only appended lines), plan a state serialiser or re-derive from stored records.
